rules.description: All 20 expected CIKs are present in the raw table
rules.sql: SELECT 20 - COUNT(DISTINCT cik) FROM raw.xbrl_company_facts
rules.rationale: The pipeline ingests 20 specific companies. If any CIK is missing, a fetch failed silently.

rules.description: No null values in required fields
rules.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM raw.xbrl_company_facts WHERE cik IS NULL OR concept IS NULL OR unit IS NULL OR end_date IS NULL OR val IS NULL OR accession_number IS NULL OR filed_date IS NULL
rules.rationale: These 7 fields define the fact grain and value — nulls indicate a parsing or flattening bug

rules.description: CIK is a positive integer
rules.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM raw.xbrl_company_facts WHERE cik <= 0
rules.rationale: SEC CIKs are positive integers. Zero or negative indicates data corruption.

rules.description: Accession numbers match SEC format (NNNNNNNNNN-NN-NNNNNN)
rules.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM raw.xbrl_company_facts WHERE accession_number NOT SIMILAR TO '[0-9]{10}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{6}'
rules.rationale: SEC accession numbers follow a strict format. Non-matching values indicate a parsing error or corrupted source data.

rules.description: No facts with filed_date in the future
rules.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM raw.xbrl_company_facts WHERE filed_date > CURRENT_DATE
rules.rationale: SEC filings are always historical. Future dates indicate data corruption or clock skew.

rules.description: All val values are finite (no NaN or Inf)
rules.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM raw.xbrl_company_facts WHERE isnan(val) OR isinf(val)
rules.rationale: NaN/Inf values break downstream calculations. Should be caught at ingest.

rules.description: Each CIK has at least 100 facts
rules.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT cik, COUNT(*) as cnt FROM raw.xbrl_company_facts GROUP BY cik HAVING COUNT(*) < 100) sub
rules.rationale: Every public company has hundreds of XBRL facts. Fewer than 100 suggests a truncated or failed fetch.

rules.description: Latest filed_date is within last 2 years
rules.sql: SELECT CASE WHEN MAX(filed_date) >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '2 years' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END FROM raw.xbrl_company_facts
rules.rationale: If the most recent filing is older than 2 years, the data source may be stale or the fetch is pulling outdated snapshots.

rules.description: label and description are populated for >99% of facts
rules.sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN label IS NOT NULL AND description IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) FROM raw.xbrl_company_facts
rules.rationale: EDA: 2,437 of 547,398 rows (0.4%) missing both label and description. 99.6% populated. Threshold 99% accommodates the gap. Source: raw-xbrl-company-facts-eda.md

rules.description: fiscal_period is one of FY, Q1, Q2, Q3 (or NULL for 8-K)
rules.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM raw.xbrl_company_facts WHERE fiscal_period IS NOT NULL AND fiscal_period NOT IN ('FY', 'Q1', 'Q2', 'Q3')
rules.rationale: EDA: only 4 distinct values observed (FY, Q1, Q2, Q3). 2,516 NULLs are 8-K filings (expected). Any other value indicates parsing error. Source: raw-xbrl-company-facts-eda.md

rules.description: form is a known SEC filing type
rules.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM raw.xbrl_company_facts WHERE form NOT IN ('10-K', '10-Q', '8-K', '10-K/A', '10-Q/A')
rules.rationale: EDA: exactly 5 distinct form values observed. Any other value indicates an unexpected filing type. Source: raw-xbrl-company-facts-eda.md

rules.description: end_date is within 6 years of filed_date for >99% of facts
rules.sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN end_date <= filed_date + INTERVAL '2192 days' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) FROM raw.xbrl_company_facts
rules.rationale: EDA found 35 facts with end_date >1 year after filed_date — all legitimate (LongTermDebtMaturities, IntangibleAssetsAmortization report forward-looking schedules up to 5 years out). Relaxed to P1 with 6-year window and 99% threshold. Source: @dq-rule-writer investigation of RAW-CF-012 P0 failure.

rules.description: load_date is never null
rules.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM raw.xbrl_company_facts WHERE load_date IS NULL
rules.rationale: load_date is a structural system-time column. Must always be populated. Source: base-zone-eda.md

rules.description: No full row duplicates (all columns identical)
rules.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT cik, entity_name, taxonomy, concept, unit, start_date, end_date, val, accession_number, fiscal_year, fiscal_period, form, filed_date, COUNT(*) as cnt FROM raw.xbrl_company_facts GROUP BY cik, entity_name, taxonomy, concept, unit, start_date, end_date, val, accession_number, fiscal_year, fiscal_period, form, filed_date HAVING COUNT(*) > 1) dupes
rules.rationale: Chaos monkey injected 3,923 full row duplicates — zero caught. Real data has legitimate multi-value facts on the same grain but NOT identical rows across all columns. Full-row dupes indicate copy/paste corruption.

rules.description: No rows with identical (cik, concept, unit, end_date, val, accession_number)
rules.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT cik, concept, unit, end_date, val, accession_number, COUNT(*) as cnt FROM raw.xbrl_company_facts GROUP BY cik, concept, unit, end_date, val, accession_number HAVING COUNT(*) > 3) dupes
rules.rationale: Real data has up to 3 legitimate copies per grain (amendments, multi-period reports). But >3 copies of the same (cik, concept, unit, end_date, val, accession_number) indicates bulk injection.

rules.description: start_date is before or equal to end_date when both are present
rules.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM raw.xbrl_company_facts WHERE start_date IS NOT NULL AND end_date IS NOT NULL AND start_date > end_date
rules.rationale: Chaos monkey injected 1,853 date inversions (start_date=2099, end_date=2000) — zero caught. A reporting period cannot end before it starts.

rules.description: fiscal_year is within 8 years of end_date year when both are present
rules.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM raw.xbrl_company_facts WHERE fiscal_year IS NOT NULL AND end_date IS NOT NULL AND ABS(fiscal_year - EXTRACT(YEAR FROM end_date)) > 8
rules.rationale: Real data has fiscal years up to 7 years from end_date (forward-looking schedules). Chaos monkey injected fy=1999 with end_date=2024 (25-year gap). 8-year window catches garbage while allowing legitimate forward schedules.

rules.description: Values for balance-sheet concepts are > $1000 for known large-cap companies
rules.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM raw.xbrl_company_facts WHERE concept IN ('Assets', 'Liabilities', 'StockholdersEquity', 'Revenues', 'CostOfRevenue') AND unit = 'USD' AND fiscal_period = 'FY' AND ABS(val) < 1000 AND ABS(val) > 0
rules.rationale: Chaos monkey injected 1,869 implausible values ($1 for Apple's revenue) — zero caught. All 20 companies are large-cap; core financial line items should never be under $1000 on annual filings.

rules.description: Assets and Revenue are never negative
rules.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM raw.xbrl_company_facts WHERE concept IN ('Assets', 'Revenues', 'CashAndCashEquivalentsAtCarryingValue') AND val < 0
rules.rationale: Chaos monkey injected 1,888 negative absolute metrics — zero caught. Total assets, revenue, and cash cannot be negative by accounting definition.

rules.description: No val values exceeding $100 trillion (1e14) in absolute terms
rules.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM raw.xbrl_company_facts WHERE ABS(val) > 1e14
rules.rationale: Chaos monkey injected 1,290 extreme outliers (val=999,999,999,999,999) — zero caught. The entire US GDP is ~$28 trillion. No single company fact should exceed $100 trillion.

rules.description: fiscal_year is between 1990 and next year when present
rules.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM raw.xbrl_company_facts WHERE fiscal_year IS NOT NULL AND (fiscal_year < 1990 OR fiscal_year > EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CURRENT_DATE) + 1)
rules.rationale: Chaos monkey injected 1,247 impossible fiscal years (1850) — zero caught. XBRL EDGAR data starts in the 2000s; 1990 allows generous buffer. No future fiscal years beyond next year.

rules.description: ingested_at is never in the future
rules.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM raw.xbrl_company_facts WHERE ingested_at > CURRENT_TIMESTAMP + INTERVAL '1 hour'
rules.rationale: Chaos monkey injected 2,002 future timestamps (ingested_at=2099) — zero caught. The 1-hour buffer handles timezone/clock skew. Anything beyond that is data corruption.

rules.description: filed_date is after 1993 (SEC EDGAR inception)
rules.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM raw.xbrl_company_facts WHERE filed_date < '1993-01-01'
rules.rationale: Chaos monkey injected 1,981 ancient dates (filed_date=1900) — zero caught. SEC EDGAR launched in 1993. No filing can predate the system.

rules.description: Total row count is within 5% of expected baseline (547,398)
rules.sql: SELECT CASE WHEN COUNT(*) BETWEEN 520000 AND 575000 THEN 0 ELSE 1 END FROM raw.xbrl_company_facts
rules.rationale: Baseline: 547,398 rows across 20 companies. A 5% swing (27K rows) accommodates normal growth. Chaos monkey injected 38K rows (7% increase) — this trips the upper bound. Major volume changes require investigation.

rules.description: Every CIK in raw data is one of the 20 expected companies
rules.rationale: Chaos monkey injected orphan CIKs (9999999, 8888888) — zero caught. The pipeline ingests exactly 20 companies. Any other CIK indicates injection, corruption, or a fetch targeting the wrong endpoint.

rules.description: taxonomy is one of the known XBRL taxonomies
rules.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM raw.xbrl_company_facts WHERE taxonomy NOT IN ('us-gaap', 'dei', 'srt', 'invest')
rules.rationale: Chaos monkey injected fake taxonomies ('fake-gaap-2099'). Only 4 taxonomies exist in our data. Unknown taxonomies indicate injection or corruption.

rules.description: Every CIK has at least one FY (annual) fact
rules.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT DISTINCT cik FROM raw.xbrl_company_facts EXCEPT SELECT DISTINCT cik FROM raw.xbrl_company_facts WHERE fiscal_period = 'FY') missing
rules.rationale: Chaos monkey injected a fake CIK with only quarterly data — zero caught. Every public company files 10-Ks (annual). A CIK with zero FY rows means incomplete data or fake CIK.

rules.description: At least 80% of facts have unit = USD, shares, pure, or USD/shares
rules.sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN unit IN ('USD', 'shares', 'pure', 'USD/shares') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) FROM raw.xbrl_company_facts
rules.rationale: Chaos monkey injected rows with 'FAKE_CURRENCY' — zero caught. Our 20 US companies should overwhelmingly report in USD. Coverage below 80% indicates bulk injection or data source change.
